В США, как оказалось, «не видят никаких проблем» в мобилизации женщин на Украине. «Женщины воюют не хуже мужчин, – заявил украинским журналистам бывший спецпосланник президента США по Украине Кит Келлог. – Моя жена воевала в Гренаде, а дочь — в Афганистане». Правда, и жена, и дочь Келлога предпочитали проводить время службы не в окопах, а в штабах. Но дело даже не в этом. Выход в окно Овертона К тому, что мобилизация женщин скоро начнется, украинцев «прогревают» уже давно. Но что тогда произойдет со страной, в которой с 2022 года население и так уменьшилось в 1,5 раза? Сказались и фронтовые потери, и сокращение территорий, и отток населения в страны Европы (откуда украинцы возвращаться не хотят). Кроме того, в разгар военных действий закономерно падает рождаемость. title: Finland has deported 155 Russian citizens this year, outpacing 2025
text: Finland has deported 155 Russian citizens this year, outpacing 2025 August 24, 2026, 6:07 pm Source: Vot Tak Finland has deported 155 Russian nationals since the start of 2026, Chief Superintendent Janne Lepsu of Finland’s National Police Board told the Russian-language outlet Vot Tak — up from more than the 104 people expelled in the first nine months of 2025. Finnish authorities sent 90 of the deportees to Russia and another 65 to other countries. Of the 155, 17 were deported under escort. “Russian nationals most often face deportation after the Finnish Immigration Service denies them a residence permit,” Lepsu said. “In 2026, though, there were about 15 to 20 deportation decisions tied to criminal activity by Russian citizens in Finland.” In 2026, Finnish authorities began deporting Russians directly across the closed border. Previously, deportees were driven to Estonia and sent across to the Russian side from there. Valery Klepkin, a journalist based in Finland, said the Russians sent home are those whose passports have expired. Without a valid document, deporting them anywhere else is difficult. text: Russia's second-biggest online retailer targeted in Ukrainian strikes Image source, Reuters By James Gregory Published 7 hours ago Warehouses belonging to Russia's second-largest online retailer have been hit by a wave of Ukrainian drone strikes. Ozon said its logistics facilities in the southern regions of Krasnodar, Dagestan, Stavropol and Adygea were on fire and several people had been injured following overnight strikes. Ukraine has for weeks struck sites belonging to Wildberries, the country's biggest online retailer, describing the firm as a legitimate target because it supplied components to the military, which Moscow denies. Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Saturday that Ukraine had opened "Pandora's box" by striking economic targets and that Russia would hit back at Kyiv's "most sensitive economic sectors". Russia has targeted Ukraine's civilian infrastructure since launching its full-scale invasion in 2022, and recent Russian attacks have hit Ukrainian warehouses and cargo terminals. Ми відверто й детально обговорили міжнародну та внутрішню політику. Антоніу добре поінформований про першочергові потреби нашого захисту, передусім в антибалістиці та фінансовій підтримці вже на найближчі місяці. Обговорили також, як ЄС може допомогти українському експорту пройти через російські терористичні удари по портах і сільському господарству. text: Прем’єр-міністр Люксембургу Люк Фріден у день нашої незалежності – з нами, поруч, в Україні. І це дійсно сильний і потрібний сигнал підтримки нашим людям, кожному, хто цю незалежність відстоює щодня. Разом із Прем’єр-міністром обговорили підсумки засідання Коаліції охочих, і головні питання – як забезпечити стійкість нашої країни цієї осені та зими. Я детально описав виклики, що потребують оперативної роботи, – фінансування армії та дефіцит бюджету. Важливо, що Люксембург готовий допомогти з пошуками рішень на двосторонньому та багатосторонньому рівнях у ЄС. Вдячний також за готовність допомогти на гуманітарному треку – з відбудовою університетських гуртожитків. Це про нашу молодь та майбутнє нашої країни передусім. Дякую!

text: 📝 В мировом океане — самая высокая температура в истории наблюдений. И это еще не настало лето в Южном полушарии Замеры европейской службы по климатическим измерениям Copernicus показывают, что средняя температура морской поверхности за пределами полярных регионов в минувшую субботу поднялась до 21,1 градуса Цельсия. Это выше предыдущего рекорда в 21,09 градуса, зафиксированного в течение трех отдельных дней в марте 2024 года. И это — гораздо выше средних значений для августа. Потепление океана может иметь далеко идущие последствия. Оно может способствовать экстремальным погодным явлением, вызывает общий рост уровня моря и наносит вред морской фауне. 🔗 Подробнее: https://bbc.in/4wQhzoC 🔗 Сайт без VPN | YouTube | Рассылка | Новое приложение BBC World Service

text: О рабочем визите Министра просвещения Российской Федерации С.С.Кравцова в Республику Южная Осетия 24 августа с.г. Посол России в Южной Осетии М.М.Кулахметов сопровождал Министра просвещения Российской Федерации С.С.Кравцова в ходе его рабочей поездки в Южную Осетию. В рамках встречи глава Минпросвещения и исполняющий обязанности Президента Республики Южная Осетия М.А.Камболов подписали план реализации совместных образовательных проектов Российской Федерации и Республики Южная Осетия на 2026–2027 годы. С.С.Кравцов торжественно передал М.А.Камболову сертификат на оснащение Цхинвальского медицинского училища им. В.Н.Карсанова необходимым оборудованием, инвентарем и учебной литературой. Он также посетил церемонию открытия представительства РГПУ им. А.И.Герцена, а также осмотрел обновленный детский технопарк «Сила ума». В 2026 году реализуется второй этап его оснащения. Предусмотрена поставка более 500 единиц оборудования по направлениям: «Хай-тек», «Робототехника», «ИТ» и «Медиапроизводство».

text: Ограбления музеев в Европе становятся все более жестокими — Европол Преступники все чаще используют при нападениях на музеи кувалды, взрывчатку и огнестрельное оружие, следует из нового доклада Европола. Если раньше похитители культурных ценностей в основном старались действовать без насилия, то теперь они все чаще применяют силу, в том числе для устрашения сотрудников музеев. Меняются и цели налетчиков. Их все больше интересуют драгоценные металлы, камни и культурно значимые артефакты, которые пользуются высоким спросом и сравнительно легко продаются нелегально. Европол отмечает появление новых группировок: некоторых участников набирают через соцсети, а к музейным кражам подключаются преступники из других сфер, которых привлекает возможность получить большую прибыль при относительно небольшом риске. В докладе упоминаются кража дакийских артефактов в Нидерландах и ограбление Лувра в 2025 году, а также нападение на парижский музей Коньяк-Жэ в 2024-м. 🎉 Подписывайся на Readovka в МАКС

text: Миру предложили простить США госдолг в $40 трлн по шумерской схеме Обозреватель The New York Times Пол Винья напомнил о способе борьбы с долгами, который практиковали еще шумерские правители около 4400 лет назад. В Шумере проблему решали радикально: правители время от времени объявляли амарги — освобождение от долгов и обязательств [прим. Readovka] — и списывали долги. Это позволяло людям выйти из долгового рабства и вернуть землю, перешедшую кредиторам. Винья признает, что буквально повторить шумерскую практику сегодня невозможно из-за сложности современной финансовой системы. По его мнению, этот опыт может стать поводом пересмотреть отношение к долгам и деньгам. Повод подходящий: федеральный долг США уже перевалил за $40 трлн, а вместе с долгами компаний, штатов и американцев достигает $77 трлн при годовом ВВП страны около $32 трлн. 🎉 Подписывайся на Readovka в МАКС

text: В России ужесточат требования к электронным дорожным знакам и табло Проект нового стандарта для знаков переменной информации (ЗПИ) и динамических информационных табло (ДИТ) подготовили в РосдорНИИ. Согласно документу, ДИТ должны быть заметны с расстояния 150 метров за городом и 100 метров в населенных пунктах. Для ЗПИ установлен единый норматив в 100 метров. Яркость экранов должна автоматически меняться в зависимости от освещенности или времени суток, пишет «Ъ» со ссылкой на РосдорНИИ. Новый ГОСТ запретит мерцание экранов, которое мешает воспринимать информацию. Знаки и табло не должны быть загорожены деревьями и наружной рекламой. На ДИТ запретят анимацию и сообщения, не связанные с дорожной обстановкой. Исключение сделают для социальной рекламы о безопасности дорожного движения. 🎉 Подписывайся на Readovka в МАКС

text: В течение дня Вооруженные Силы Российской Федерации продолжали нанесение ударов по морским судам, портовой и логистической инфраструктуре Украины, задействованным в интересах ВСУ. Ударными беспилотными летательными аппаратами и высокоточным оружием воздушного базирования поражены: в порту «Одесса» – сухогруз, доставивший на Украину груз военного назначения; в порту «Южный» – три резервуара с горюче-смазочными материалами и четыре хранилища с военным имуществом, предназначенным для ВСУ, а также объекты портовой инфраструктуры, используемые для разгрузки грузов военного назначения. Кроме того, в районе Одессы нанесено поражение по двум логистическим центрам, используемым для хранения боеприпасов, вооружения и военной техники, а также военного имущества, предназначенных для обеспечения ВСУ.

text: Вдячний Прем’єр-міністру Енді Бернему за те, що перший його візит за кордон – саме до України, у день річниці відновлення нашої незалежності. Партнерство з Великою Британією для України особливе: ми побудували безпрецедентно сильний і дружній діалог, яким точно можна пишатися. Було честю від імені Українського народу передати Енді першу нову державну відзнаку «Вдячність Українського народу», присвоєну народу Сполученого Королівства. І сьогодні ми розширюємо нашу співпрацю ще більше – Україна та Велика Британія розвиватимуть партнерство у сфері штучного інтелекту. Підписали сьогодні відповідну декларацію. Під час зустрічі обговорили повний спектр співпраці: ліцензії на виробництво Storm Shadow, допомогу зі страхуванням на українському ринку, як забезпечити фінансову стійкість України, дипломатію та інші речі. Цінуємо, що курс Великої Британії незмінний – повна підтримка України й нашого захисту. Дякую, Енді! Дякую, Велика Британіє!

text: 🔥 Рятувальники продовжують боротьбу з масштабною лісовою пожежею Поблизу села Богдани Вишгородського району триває ліквідація масштабної лісової пожежі. Спекотна та вітряна погода створює надзвичайно складні умови для вогнеборців і сприяє швидкому поширенню вогню. Попри це, рятувальники продовжують боротьбу зі стихією, стримуючи поширення пожежі та захищаючи лісові масиви. 🟡 Пожежа охопила значну територію, а її фронт простягається на кілька кілометрів. До ліквідації пожежі залучені рятувальники Київщини, столиці та інших областей України, працівники ДП «Ліси України». Додатково до гасіння залучено авіацію ДСНС. У складних умовах, під палючим сонцем, у задимленні та за сильного вітру, вогнеборці продовжують працювати на межі своїх можливостей. Крок за кроком вони відстоюють ліс у боротьбі з вогнем, ризикуючи власним здоров’ям і безпекою. Це важка та виснажлива робота, яка вимагає витримки, мужності й професійності кожного, хто сьогодні стоїть на захисті лісу. title: Russia has been steering ninth-graders toward vocational college instead of regular high school. The country’s top court just ruled that one school went too far by outright refusing a student.
text: Russia has been steering ninth-graders toward vocational college instead of regular high school. The country’s top court just ruled that one school went too far by outright refusing a student. August 24, 2026, 7:49 pm Source: Supreme Court of the Russian Federation Russia’s Supreme Court — the country’s highest court of general jurisdiction — has ruled that a school unlawfully refused to let a student continue his education after ninth grade. “Successfully completing a general education is not grounds for expulsion,” the court said in its explanation. The complaint came from Valentina Berseneva, a resident of the Sverdlovsk region, whose son was denied enrollment in the 10th grade because the school organizes those classes around specialized tracks. Berseneva asked that her son be placed in a general-education class instead, the Russian business daily Kommersant said . Berseneva took the case to court, seeking to have the school director’s order expelling her son upon completion of his studies voided, but three lower courts denied her claim. title: Putin extends Alexander Bastrykin’s term as Investigative Committee chief through 2027, using a 2024 law that lets him personally extend that term past age 70
text: Putin extends Alexander Bastrykin’s term as Investigative Committee chief through 2027, using a 2024 law that lets him personally extend that term past age 70 August 24, 2026, 7:41 pm Source: Meduza Russian President Vladimir Putin has extended Alexander Bastrykin’s term as head of the Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative agency, until August 27, 2027, according to a decree published on the government’s official legal information portal. Bastrykin, who has led the agency since 2011, turns 73 on August 27. The law governing the Investigative Committee sets the maximum service age at 65 but allows it to be extended to 70 “by decision of the head [of the agency].” In 2024, Putin signed legislation granting himself the authority to extend the Investigative Committee chief’s term of service past age 70. Bastrykin has overseen every high-profile criminal case, including politically charged ones such as the Bolotnaya Square case and the prosecution of Alexei Navalny and his supporters. title: Reuters: Ukrainian drones knocked out a major Russian oil refinery in Perm for the second time this year
text: Reuters: Ukrainian drones knocked out a major Russian oil refinery in Perm for the second time this year August 24, 2026, 7:28 pm Source: Reuters The oil refinery in Perm has halted operations following a Ukrainian drone attack, two industry sources told Reuters. The sources said repairs could take up to two weeks. Ukrainian forces struck Perm with drones on the morning of August 21. Journalists later reported smoke rising over the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez plant. The sources confirmed to Reuters that the attack caused a fire at the refinery. One of the plant’s primary crude distillation units, which accounts for about 40% of the refinery’s capacity, has been shut down, according to Reuters. A second primary unit, which accounts for 34% of capacity, has been idle since July 29, the sources said. Ukrainian drones have struck the Perm refinery several times since the spring of 2026. In early May, the plant had already halted operations indefinitely. Permnefteorgsintez is one of Russia’s largest oil refineries. It ranks seventh in the country by refining volume, according to Reuters. Repeated Ukrainian strikes on oil industry facilities have kept Russia in a fuel crisis all summer. A

title: Russian woman who lived in Ukraine for more than a decade faces treason charges after returning to Moscow to replace her passport
text: Russian woman who lived in Ukraine for more than a decade faces treason charges after returning to Moscow to replace her passport August 24, 2026, 7:01 pm Source: Mediazona Authorities in Russia have opened a treason case against Svetlana Golovatenko, a Russian citizen who lived in Ukraine for more than a decade, after she flew to Moscow to renew her documents. Golovatenko was born in the town of Severoonezhsk, in Russia’s Arkhangelsk region. For more than 10 years, she lived in Kyiv, where she worked as a manicurist and pedicurist. She held a Ukrainian residence permit. Her parents and brother live in Russia. Mediazona , an independent Russian news outlet, learned that Golovatenko flew to Russia via Georgia on April 23 to replace her expired internal passport and re-register her home in Donetsk. She was detained in the arrivals hall of Moscow’s Vnukovo Airport. The next day, she was jailed for 15 days on an administrative charge of “petty hooliganism.” Police then filed seven more identical charges against her, and the cases went before several courts, including some in the Kaluga region. title: Trans man from Chechnya found dead in Batumi; relatives suspect he was killed
text: Trans man from Chechnya found dead in Batumi; relatives suspect he was killed August 24, 2026, 6:58 pm Source: Radio Svoboda Dmitry Menyaev, a 21-year-old ethnic Chechen who was born in Russia and moved to Georgia in 2022, was found dead in his apartment in Batumi on August 15, according to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty’s Russian service . It’s unclear when Menyaev died. He worked remotely and was last seen online on Telegram on August 3. Emergency responders forced open the door after neighbors complained of a strong smell. According to RFE/RL, Menyaev had undergone a gender transition. In remarks quoted by the outlet Noctu, Zviad Markoidze, a lawyer for the family, said Menyaev was a member of the LGBTQ community. Investigators have opened a criminal investigation into incitement to suicide, but Menyaev’s relatives suspect he may have been the victim of an “honor killing” or of a murder motivated by transphobia. They believe the killing could have been carried out by other relatives on the Chechen side of his family, who did not know about his transition and wrote that he “needed to get married” — using a Russian phrase that refers only to a woman taking a husband. text: Противник заявляет о реализации проекта «Маячня» , направленного на решение задач навигации и точного позиционирования дронов-перехватчиков в акватории Чёрного моря в условиях отсутствия спутниковой связи. В качестве основной цели перехвата в прибрежной полосе выступают разведывательные БПЛА, которые, помимо ведения разведки, являются ретрансляторами и частью mesh-сети для приёма и передачи сигналов для групп дронов-камикадзе. title: Russia's second-biggest online retailer targeted in Ukrainian strikes
text: Russia's second-biggest online retailer targeted in Ukrainian strikes Image source, Reuters By James Gregory Published 9 hours ago Warehouses belonging to Russia's second-largest online retailer have been hit by a wave of Ukrainian drone strikes. Ozon said its logistics facilities in the southern regions of Krasnodar, Dagestan, Stavropol and Adygea were on fire and several people had been injured following overnight strikes. Ukraine has for weeks struck sites belonging to Wildberries, the country's biggest online retailer, describing the firm as a legitimate target because it supplied components to the military, which Moscow denies. Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Saturday that Ukraine had opened "Pandora's box" by striking economic targets and that Russia would hit back at Kyiv's "most sensitive economic sectors". Russia has targeted Ukraine's civilian infrastructure since launching its full-scale invasion in 2022, and recent Russian attacks have hit Ukrainian warehouses and cargo terminals. text: Сирия приветствовала решение США исключить ее из списка спонсоров терроризма Согласно решению американских конгрессменов, с понедельника, Вашингтон больше не считает власти Сирии спонсорами терроризма. Сирийский министр иностранных дел Асад аль-Шайбани назвал это решение «исторической вехой». Глава Госдепа США Марко Рубио отметил, что таким образом Вашингтон отметил шаги сирийского правительства по полному дистанцированию от международного терроризма. Администрация Дональда Трампа установила хорошие отношения с новыми властями Сирии во главе с Ахмедом аль-Шараа — бывшим исламистским боевиком, который в конце 2024 года сверг Башара Асада. Решение об исключении Сирии из списка спонсоров терроризма поможет привлечь инвестиции в послевоенное восстановление страны. 🔗 Сайт без VPN | YouTube | Рассылка | Новое приложение BBC World Service

text: В стане противника раздрай и шатание: вор на воре, вором погоняет и вора пихает. Картина маслом, однако. Вот начался суд над Ириной Мудрой, коррупционеркой пробы негде ставить, замглавы ОП (т.н. "офис президента"). Других (некоррупционеров) у нарколыги-хазарина нет, всех подобрал под себя. На суд пришел поручителем ни кто-нибудь, а сам главный раввин Киева Йонатан Маркович. Просил-умолял слёзно за Мудрую коррупционерку, рвал пейсы и вздымал руки в гору. Мол, вэй, вэй, она своя, молилась со всеми. Мол, "не подведет ни общину, ни меня, ни государство". Шарий, конечно, ещё тот укрожук, но тут с ним не поспоришь — ему кажется, что эта группировка всё больше приобретает характер этнической ОПГ. Когда кажется, креститься надо. Только не обманут эпитеты "кажется", "напоминает", "приобретает"... Это пан Шарий так пишет, чтоб на него не сильно обиделись захватчики. А если называть вещи своими именами, без дураков, то тут ничего не попишешь – власть в Киеве захвачена именно этнической ОПГ, и упоротый бандеровский флуд мало кого может обмануть. Выдуманная история, дегенераты, твари и извращенцы возведены в ранг "хероев нации", а в ОПГ знай себе посмеиваются над аборигенами. Украинцами управля

text: 📝 Хроника специальной военной операции 📝 за 24 августа 2026 года 🧨 Российские войска в течение суток нанесли удары по логистическим и промышленным объектам в Одесской области . text: Посольство России в Боснии и Герцеговине: 18 августа Посол России И.А.Калабухов посетил муниципалитет Рогатица В ходе визита проведены переговоры с руководством муниципалитета, включая мэра Н.Прелича и Председателя Скупщины С.Янковича. 🤝 Подчёркнута важность дальнейшего развития межрегионального сотрудничества в экономической и гуманитарной сферах как важной составляющей стратегических отношений России и Республики Сербской. Отдельным пунктом программы стало посещение центральной муниципальной школы имени Святого Саввы, в рамках которого состоялась торжественная церемония передачи в дар методических пособий и электронного оборудования по линии Фонда «Русский мир». Всего Фондом выделены учебные комплекты для 27 школ Республики Сербской, где изучается русский язык, в том числе для Основной школы им.Св.Саввы и Центра средних школ «27 января» в Рогатице. Посол пообщался с директорами учебных заведений И.Новакович и Д.Йовичичем и педагогами по русскому языку, а также осмотрел русский класс.

text: Siberian Wildfires Reach 3.5M Acres Across Krasnoyarsk and Sakha Republic Aug. 24, 2026 The Forest Fire center of the Krasnoyarsk Territory Wildfires across Siberia continued to expand as blazes in the Krasnoyarsk region and the republic of Sakha grew to nearly 3.5 million acres, roughly the size of the U.S. state of Connecticut, forest fire authorities said Monday. In the Krasnoyarsk region, 128 active wildfires were burning across 405,800 hectares (1 million acres), according to the regional forest fire center. S akha, Russia’s largest ethnic republic, had 36 active blazes covering 987,067 hectares (2.44 million acres) as of midnight Monday, federal authorities said . Russia’s Aerial Forest Protection Service said more than 1.3 million hectares (3.3 million acres) of wildfires were burning across Russia. Authorities have blamed the fires on summer heat and Siberian silk moth infestations, which have killed off vast swaths of trees and left behind highly flammable deadwood. The Krasnoyarsk region declared a wildfire emergency on June 10, barring the public from entering woodlands, lighting campfires, burning trash or grass and conducting any other fire-hazardous work. text: Russian Government Proposes Tax Relief for Wildberries and Sellers After Drone Attacks Aug. 24, 2026 A Wildberries warehouse in Moscow region on fire after Ukrainian drone attack. REUTERS / Stringer The Russian government has drafted a financial assistance package for online retailer Wildberries and sellers who use the platform following weeks of Ukrainian attacks on the company’s warehouses and logistics centers, the Finance Ministry said Monday. Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said the proposed measures include a deferral of taxes and insurance payments, as well as a freeze on tax audits , all with the aim of “easing administrative and financial pressure” on impacted businesses. Under the draft proposal, sellers whose losses exceed 5% of annual revenue will receive a 12-month deferral on value-added tax (VAT), corporate tax and other liabilities due between August 2026 and July 2027. Following the deferral period, Wildberries sellers will be allowed to settle their tax obligations in equal monthly installments over 12 months. The decision by the court’s conservative majority, with its liberal members dissenting, appears to leave room for additional court challenges that could prevent the implementation of the new restrictions in time for the upcoming midterm elections in November, with some states beginning to send mail ballots to voters in just a few weeks. The case could be one of multiple voting-related challenges before the justices. The justice department had filed an emergency appeal asking the high court to allow work on implementing the changes before the midterms. Trump’s executive order, signed in March, calls on his administration to create lists of eligible voters and orders the US Postal Service (USPS) to deliver mail ballots only to people on those lists. The USPS is prepared to publish a new rule this week to implement that change.

title: Burnham vows support for Ukraine despite 'outrageous threats' from Russia
text: Burnham vows support for Ukraine despite 'outrageous threats' from Russia Figure caption, Is UK's Storm Shadow missile a game changer for Ukraine? By Henry Moore Â and Â Imogen James Published 24 August 2026, 00:07 BST Updated 5 hours ago Andy Burnham has promised to keep up the pressure on Russia despite Moscow's "outrageous threats", on his first official visit to Ukraine as UK prime minister. Burnham met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and chaired his first meeting of the "coalition of the willing", set up by the UK and France under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer. He said the coalition was "doing everything we can" while urging the US Congress to "ratchet up" economic pressure on Russia. The government has agreed to hand over blueprints for British-made components for the Scalp missile, a French version of the UK's Storm Shadow cruise missile - allowing Ukraine to produce the long-range weapon domestically. title: Australia news live: WA to get Blue Poles in painting’s first interstate trip in two decades; power line repairs cause Sydney trains chaos
text: 17.54 EDT Jackson Pollock masterpiece Blue Poles to visit Perth Tom McIlroy One of the crown jewels of the National Gallery of Australia’s collection, Blue Poles by Jackson Pollock, will go on display in Western Australia for the first time next year. During a campaigning swing through electorally sensitive WA, the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, will on Tuesday announce a loan of the massive work to the Art Gallery of Western Australia in Perth from April to September 2027. It is the painting’s first interstate tour since it featured at the NGV’s 20th anniversary exhibition in 2003/4. The painting will be loaned as part of a program designed to share key items from Australia’s national cultural collection and coincides with badly needed upgrade works at the NGA in Canberra. Blue Poles (1952). Photograph: Andy Rain/EPA The Whitlam government sensationally bought the painting in 1973 for $1.4m, but it is now insured for more than $500m. When sold, it was the highest price paid for an American work of art. “Blue Poles changed our nation, so it makes sense that the nation gets to see it,” Albanese said: The national collection belongs to every Australian – no matter where they live.
author: Nick Visser

title: NAACP denounces supreme court decision to allow Trump administration to restrict mail-in voting – live
text: 18.07 EDT Trump knows Republicans 'are unpopular and will lose in a free and fair election', NAACP says The president of the NAACP, which sued Donald Trump in April to block his order to restrict mail-in voting, denounced the supreme court decision that allows the order to be implemented, despite claims that it is illegal and unconstitutional. The NAACP president, Derrick Johnson , said in a statement: “Let this ruling be a reminder that democracy is never, ever, guaranteed. We have to fight for it, we have to fight to keep it, and we have to protect the rights we do have within it. Those in power know full well that they are unpopular and will lose in a free and fair election, and so they are trying to do everything they possibly can to make it difficult for you to vote. Trump’s order has nothing to do with election integrity. It has everything to do with maintaining power at all costs.”

title: Australia news live: Coles blames competitor’s Ooshies for slowing sales; young people the first generation to earn less than their parents at same age
text: 19.36 EDT Coles blames Ooshies for hurting its sales as it reports $1.09bn profit Luca Ittimani Coles reported growing profit from its supermarkets despite a slump in alcohol sales and a delayed hit from Woolworths’ Disney “Ooshie” giveaways. The company today said it grown supermarket sales by 3.7% and gained market share over the year to June. Growth had continued into July but slumped amid a “competitor’s collectibles campaign” – a reference to the “Ooshie” plastic figurines. Coles said its digital sales boomed 26.4%, to $5.6bn, helped by a partnership with Uber Eats and improved wait times for store-based click and collect orders. Its own-brand product sales grew 6.1%, with the company singling out its cleaning, baby and ready meal range. The company said the prices of its supermarket products rose just 1.5% through the year. Supermarkets’ own calculation methods for inflation are not necessarily intuitive. Its net profit bumped up 1% to $1.09bn as a result. Profit would have been $1.25bn if not for a penalty from a federal court ruling over its payment of managers . But liquor sales fell 3.3% from the prior year. title: Gavin Newsom says California will sue Trump administration again to block ‘Orwellian rules’ meant to curb mail-in voting – live
text: 19.17 EDT California plans to sue again to stop Trump from restricting mail voting and could make blocking delivery a felony California’s governor, Gavin Newsom, said on Monday that his state would sue the Trump administration again to block federal changes to mail voting, after the US supreme court ruled that a previous suit was filed too early in the process by his state and 22 others. “California will be suing AGAIN to block these Orwellian rules from being implemented,” Newsom posted . Newsom also highlighted two new proposed state laws that would make it a crime to interfere with the delivery of mail ballots. In a press release, Newsom added that he and the California legislature “are doubling down to ensure California continues to defend democracy as new threats from Donald Trump and his election-rigging allies emerge”. Two draft laws would establish three new felonies under California state law, punishable by up to four years in prison. text: Advertising What the renewed Black Sea blockade means for Ukraine’s farmers Explainer Europe As Ukraine and Russia hammer each other’s Black Sea ports, the amount of grain being shipped through the crucial waterway has slowed to a crawl. title: Ukraine's UN rep says Russia is losing war against Ukraine
text: Ukraine's UN rep says Russia is losing war against Ukraine Olha Hlushchenko — 25 August, 02:36 Andrii Melnyk. Photo: Facebook Посилання скопійовано Add UP as preferred source in Google Andrii Melnyk, Ukraine's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, has said that Russia is losing the war it started and that its economy is coming under increasing strain from military spending, sanctions and Ukrainian strikes. Source: Melnyk speaking at a UN Security Council meeting held on Ukraine's Independence Day, as reported by Ukrinform Quote: "Irrespective of all the barbaric attacks against civilians in Ukraine, Russia is losing and will lose this war." Advertisement: Details: Melnyk pointed to the dismissal of Andrei Klepach, chief economist at VEB.RF, Russia's second-largest state-owned bank, reportedly on the Kremlin's direct orders after he made critical remarks about the state of the Russian economy. Klepach had warned, among other things, that Moscow would not be able to win a prolonged economic war against Ukraine. title: Russian drone attack damages 16-storey building in Kyiv
text: Russian drone attack damages 16-storey building in Kyiv Olha Hlushchenko — 25 August, 00:30 Column of smoke. Stock photo: Suspilne Посилання скопійовано Add UP as preferred source in Google A 16-storey residential building has been damaged in a Russian drone attack on Kyiv's Holosiivskyi district on the night of 24-25 August. Source: Kyiv City Military Administration ; Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko Quote from Kyiv City Military Administration: "A 16-storey residential building in Holosiivskyi district has been damaged as a result of the enemy attack. Advertisement: Services are heading to the site. Further information is being confirmed." Details: Following Kyiv City Military Administration's report, monitoring Telegram channels reported further explosions in Kyiv. Update: Klitschko later said that falling drone debris had caused walls to collapse in the 16-storey residential building in the Holosiivskyi district. Windows were also blown out on the 13th floor. title: Ukraine's UN rep says Russia is losing war against Ukraine
text: Ukraine's UN rep says Russia is losing war against Ukraine Olha Hlushchenko — 25 August, 02:36 Andrii Melnyk. Photo: Facebook Посилання скопійовано Add UP as preferred source in Google Andrii Melnyk, Ukraine's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, has said that Russia is losing the war it started and that its economy is coming under increasing strain from military spending, sanctions and Ukrainian strikes. Source: Melnyk speaking at a UN Security Council meeting held on Ukraine's Independence Day, as reported by Ukrinform Quote: "Irrespective of all the barbaric attacks against civilians in Ukraine, Russia is losing and will lose this war." Advertisement: Details: Melnyk pointed to the dismissal of Andrei Klepach, chief economist at VEB.RF, Russia's second-largest state-owned bank, reportedly on the Kremlin's direct orders after he made critical remarks about the state of the Russian economy. title: Russia attacks Red Cross warehouse in Kherson, causing nearly US$627,000 in damage – photos
text: Russia attacks Red Cross warehouse in Kherson, causing nearly US$627,000 in damage – photos Olha Hlushchenko — 25 August, 02:00 Photo: Ukrainian Red Cross on social media Посилання скопійовано Add UP as preferred source in Google A Russian drone attack on the evening of 23 August caused a fire at a Ukrainian Red Cross warehouse in Kherson, with damage to humanitarian supplies estimated at nearly UAH 28 million (about US$627,000). Source : Ukrainian Red Cross on Facebook Details : The organisation said the fire had damaged and destroyed humanitarian supplies stored at the warehouse worth nearly UAH 28 million. Advertisement: Photo: Ukrainian Red Cross on social media The destroyed supplies included equipment and materials intended for preparations for the autumn and winter period, as well as emergency response stocks for dealing with the aftermath of attacks, including materials for temporarily covering damaged buildings. Photo: Ukrainian Red Cross on social media The warehouse also contained medical supplies, blankets, hygiene kits, equipment for providing water and electricity, and other humanitarian aid. text: Ex-Pussy Riot Member Says She Helped the FSB Spy on Kremlin Critics Aug. 24, 2026 Rita Flores. Social media Former Pussy Riot member Rita Flores has revealed that she was coerced into working as an informant for Russia’s FSB security service, saying that she gathered information on anti-war activists and was involved in a failed assassination plot against an exiled Kremlin critic. Flores said FSB officers coerced her into signing a cooperation agreement following a February 2023 raid on her Moscow apartment, threatening her with criminal prosecution over social media posts about alleged Russian war crimes in Ukraine alongside death threats against her relatives. “They began recruiting me with all kinds of threats and abuse [including] threats to murder my family and that I’d never be able to prove who killed my mother,” she told the exiled news outlet Port in a video interview. Operating under the codename “Harley,” Flores said she was assigned to build detailed profiles on Russian artists and political dissidents. text: Putin Signs Order Allowing Government to Seize Critical Infrastructure Following Attacks Aug. 24, 2026 Vladimir Putin. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin on Monday granted the government powers to take control of critically important infrastructure sites if they are deemed to be poorly protected against Ukrainian strikes and other threats. The special powers, set out in an executive order , allow the state to assume control over the physical, financial and legal assets of facilities that fail to maintain adequate security or are slow to make repairs following attacks. Putin's order encompasses a wide array of sectors, including fuel, energy, industrial, communications, transportation and commercial logistics sites deemed essential to national security and economic stability. The new powers come a week after the president instructed the government to help rebuild commercial warehouses that have been damaged in Ukrainian attacks. text: Russia Is Betting on the MC-21 to Reverse Its Aviation Decline. It’s No Silver Bullet. By Sascha Roslyakov Aug. 24, 2026 President Vladimir Putin visits an aviation plant in Irkutsk. Sputnik / Vyacheslav Prokofyev / Pool via REUTERS This article was first published by VPost. It took 21 years for President Vladimir Putin to step aboard Russia’s new MC-21 passenger jet, the long-delayed plane that Moscow hopes will replace the aging Airbus and Boeing aircraft underpinning its commercial fleet. But the plane Putin inspected at the Irkutsk Aviation Plant in July was markedly different from the aircraft that was originally envisioned. Western sanctions imposed after Russia invaded Ukraine forced manufacturer United Aircraft Corporation to replace its foreign-made engines, composite wing and other components with Russian alternatives. text: Kremlin Says It’s Working to Minimize Impact of Ukrainian Attacks on Russian Grain Exports By Reuters Aug. 24, 2026 Grain is loaded onto a ship at the port of Novorossiysk in southern Russia. Ivan Studenov (CC BY-SA 4.0) The Kremlin said on Monday that measures were being taken to minimize the impact of Ukrainian strikes on Russia 's grain exports as global wheat importers brace for tighter supplies amid attacks on Black Sea grain infrastructure. Tit-for-tat attacks by Russia and Ukraine, both major grain exporters, on ports and vessels in recent weeks have shuttered grain terminals and forced shippers to delay or cancel loadings for dozens of cargoes during the peak export season. "Measures have been identified and will be further developed, ensuring that all grain intended for export is shipped on time and in full," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters, without providing further details. President Vladimir Putin acknowledged last week that Russia was experiencing problems with its agricultural exports, but said officials would work to resolve them. title: Siberian Wildfires Reach 3.5M Acres Across Krasnoyarsk and Sakha Republic
text: Siberian Wildfires Reach 3.5M Acres Across Krasnoyarsk and Sakha Republic Aug. 24, 2026 The Forest Fire center of the Krasnoyarsk Territory Wildfires across Siberia continued to expand as blazes in the Krasnoyarsk region and the republic of Sakha grew to nearly 3.5 million acres, roughly the size of the U.S. state of Connecticut, forest fire authorities said Monday. In the Krasnoyarsk region, 128 active wildfires were burning across 405,800 hectares (1 million acres), according to the regional forest fire center. S akha, Russia’s largest ethnic republic, had 36 active blazes covering 987,067 hectares (2.44 million acres) as of midnight Monday, federal authorities said . Russia’s Aerial Forest Protection Service said more than 1.3 million hectares (3.3 million acres) of wildfires were burning across Russia. Authorities have blamed the fires on summer heat and Siberian silk moth infestations, which have killed off vast swaths of trees and left behind highly flammable deadwood. The Krasnoyarsk region declared a wildfire emergency on June 10, barring the public from entering woodlands, lighting campfires, burning trash or grass and conducting any other fire-hazardous work. title: Russian Government Proposes Tax Relief for Wildberries and Sellers After Drone Attacks
text: Russian Government Proposes Tax Relief for Wildberries and Sellers After Drone Attacks Aug. 24, 2026 A Wildberries warehouse in Moscow region on fire after Ukrainian drone attack. REUTERS / Stringer The Russian government has drafted a financial assistance package for online retailer Wildberries and sellers who use the platform following weeks of Ukrainian attacks on the company’s warehouses and logistics centers, the Finance Ministry said Monday. Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said the proposed measures include a deferral of taxes and insurance payments, as well as a freeze on tax audits , all with the aim of “easing administrative and financial pressure” on impacted businesses. Under the draft proposal, sellers whose losses exceed 5% of annual revenue will receive a 12-month deferral on value-added tax (VAT), corporate tax and other liabilities due between August 2026 and July 2027. Following the deferral period, Wildberries sellers will be allowed to settle their tax obligations in equal monthly installments over 12 months. title: Russian Government Proposes Tax Relief for Wildberries and Sellers After Drone Attacks
text: Russian Government Proposes Tax Relief for Wildberries and Sellers After Drone Attacks Aug. 24, 2026 A Wildberries warehouse in Moscow region on fire after Ukrainian drone attack. REUTERS / Stringer The Russian government has drafted a financial assistance package for online retailer Wildberries and sellers who use the platform following weeks of Ukrainian attacks on the company’s warehouses and logistics centers, the Finance Ministry said Monday. Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said the proposed measures include a deferral of taxes and insurance payments, as well as a freeze on tax audits , all with the aim of “easing administrative and financial pressure” on impacted businesses. Under the draft proposal, sellers whose losses exceed 5% of annual revenue will receive a 12-month deferral on value-added tax (VAT), corporate tax and other liabilities due between August 2026 and July 2027. Following the deferral period, Wildberries sellers will be allowed to settle their tax obligations in equal monthly installments over 12 months. title: Ex-Pussy Riot Member Says She Helped the FSB Spy on Kremlin Critics
text: Ex-Pussy Riot Member Says She Helped the FSB Spy on Kremlin Critics Aug. 24, 2026 Rita Flores. Social media Former Pussy Riot member Rita Flores has revealed that she was coerced into working as an informant for Russia’s FSB security service, saying that she gathered information on anti-war activists and was involved in a failed assassination plot against an exiled Kremlin critic. Flores said FSB officers coerced her into signing a cooperation agreement following a February 2023 raid on her Moscow apartment, threatening her with criminal prosecution over social media posts about alleged Russian war crimes in Ukraine alongside death threats against her relatives. “They began recruiting me with all kinds of threats and abuse [including] threats to murder my family and that I’d never be able to prove who killed my mother,” she told the exiled news outlet Port in a video interview. Operating under the codename “Harley,” Flores said she was assigned to build detailed profiles on Russian artists and political dissidents. text: Putin Signs Order Allowing Government to Seize Critical Infrastructure Following Attacks Aug. 24, 2026 Vladimir Putin. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin on Monday granted the government powers to take control of critically important infrastructure sites if they are deemed to be poorly protected against Ukrainian strikes and other threats. The special powers, set out in an executive order , allow the state to assume control over the physical, financial and legal assets of facilities that fail to maintain adequate security or are slow to make repairs following attacks. Putin's order encompasses a wide array of sectors, including fuel, energy, industrial, communications, transportation and commercial logistics sites deemed essential to national security and economic stability. The new powers come a week after the president instructed the government to help rebuild commercial warehouses that have been damaged in Ukrainian attacks. text: Russia Is Betting on the MC-21 to Reverse Its Aviation Decline. It’s No Silver Bullet. By Sascha Roslyakov Aug. 24, 2026 President Vladimir Putin visits an aviation plant in Irkutsk. Sputnik / Vyacheslav Prokofyev / Pool via REUTERS This article was first published by VPost. It took 21 years for President Vladimir Putin to step aboard Russia’s new MC-21 passenger jet, the long-delayed plane that Moscow hopes will replace the aging Airbus and Boeing aircraft underpinning its commercial fleet. But the plane Putin inspected at the Irkutsk Aviation Plant in July was markedly different from the aircraft that was originally envisioned. Western sanctions imposed after Russia invaded Ukraine forced manufacturer United Aircraft Corporation to replace its foreign-made engines, composite wing and other components with Russian alternatives. The MC-21’s troubled development reflects the mounting pressure on Russian civil aviation after sanctions forced manufacturers to redesign aircraft using heavier and costlier domestic components, while airlines increasingly rely on aging Western-made planes kept flying through improvised supply chains. text: Kremlin Says It’s Working to Minimize Impact of Ukrainian Attacks on Russian Grain Exports By Reuters Aug. 24, 2026 Grain is loaded onto a ship at the port of Novorossiysk in southern Russia. Ivan Studenov (CC BY-SA 4.0) The Kremlin said on Monday that measures were being taken to minimize the impact of Ukrainian strikes on Russia 's grain exports as global wheat importers brace for tighter supplies amid attacks on Black Sea grain infrastructure. Tit-for-tat attacks by Russia and Ukraine, both major grain exporters, on ports and vessels in recent weeks have shuttered grain terminals and forced shippers to delay or cancel loadings for dozens of cargoes during the peak export season. text: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Dr. Frank Ledwidge, former military intelligence officer and Senior Lecturer in Strategy at Portsmouth University. According to Dr. Ledwidge, the latest European commitments to Ukraine are merely politically symbolic. He warns that the coalition is failing to address Kyiv's most urgent problem: air defence. Ukraine needs interceptors capable of defeating Russian ballistic and hypersonic missiles, The war-torn country remains exposed to attacks on its defence industry and Russia’s ruthless campaign against civil energy infrastructure as winter approaches.

title: Ex-Pussy Riot Member Says She Helped the FSB Spy on Kremlin Critics
text: Ex-Pussy Riot Member Says She Helped the FSB Spy on Kremlin Critics Aug. 24, 2026 Rita Flores. Social media Former Pussy Riot member Rita Flores has revealed that she was coerced into working as an informant for Russia’s FSB security service, saying that she gathered information on anti-war activists and was involved in a failed assassination plot against an exiled Kremlin critic. Flores said FSB officers coerced her into signing a cooperation agreement following a February 2023 raid on her Moscow apartment, threatening her with criminal prosecution over social media posts about alleged Russian war crimes in Ukraine alongside death threats against her relatives. “They began recruiting me with all kinds of threats and abuse [including] threats to murder my family and that I’d never be able to prove who killed my mother,” she told the exiled news outlet Port in a video interview. Operating under the codename “Harley,” Flores said she was assigned to build detailed profiles on Russian artists and political dissidents. title: Putin Signs Order Allowing Government to Seize Critical Infrastructure Following Attacks
text: Putin Signs Order Allowing Government to Seize Critical Infrastructure Following Attacks Aug. 24, 2026 Vladimir Putin. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin on Monday granted the government powers to take control of critically important infrastructure sites if they are deemed to be poorly protected against Ukrainian strikes and other threats. The special powers, set out in an executive order , allow the state to assume control over the physical, financial and legal assets of facilities that fail to maintain adequate security or are slow to make repairs following attacks. Putin's order encompasses a wide array of sectors, including fuel, energy, industrial, communications, transportation and commercial logistics sites deemed essential to national security and economic stability. The new powers come a week after the president instructed the government to help rebuild commercial warehouses that have been damaged in Ukrainian attacks. text: Russia Is Betting on the MC-21 to Reverse Its Aviation Decline. It’s No Silver Bullet. By Sascha Roslyakov Aug. 24, 2026 President Vladimir Putin visits an aviation plant in Irkutsk. Sputnik / Vyacheslav Prokofyev / Pool via REUTERS This article was first published by VPost. It took 21 years for President Vladimir Putin to step aboard Russia’s new MC-21 passenger jet, the long-delayed plane that Moscow hopes will replace the aging Airbus and Boeing aircraft underpinning its commercial fleet. But the plane Putin inspected at the Irkutsk Aviation Plant in July was markedly different from the aircraft that was originally envisioned. Western sanctions imposed after Russia invaded Ukraine forced manufacturer United Aircraft Corporation to replace its foreign-made engines, composite wing and other components with Russian alternatives. text: Kremlin Says It’s Working to Minimize Impact of Ukrainian Attacks on Russian Grain Exports By Reuters Aug. 24, 2026 Grain is loaded onto a ship at the port of Novorossiysk in southern Russia. Ivan Studenov (CC BY-SA 4.0) The Kremlin said on Monday that measures were being taken to minimize the impact of Ukrainian strikes on Russia 's grain exports as global wheat importers brace for tighter supplies amid attacks on Black Sea grain infrastructure. Tit-for-tat attacks by Russia and Ukraine, both major grain exporters, on ports and vessels in recent weeks have shuttered grain terminals and forced shippers to delay or cancel loadings for dozens of cargoes during the peak export season. "Measures have been identified and will be further developed, ensuring that all grain intended for export is shipped on time and in full," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters, without providing further details. title: Siberian Wildfires Reach 3.5M Acres Across Krasnoyarsk and Sakha Republic
text: Siberian Wildfires Reach 3.5M Acres Across Krasnoyarsk and Sakha Republic Aug. 24, 2026 The Forest Fire center of the Krasnoyarsk Territory Wildfires across Siberia continued to expand as blazes in the Krasnoyarsk region and the republic of Sakha grew to nearly 3.5 million acres, roughly the size of the U.S. state of Connecticut, forest fire authorities said Monday. In the Krasnoyarsk region, 128 active wildfires were burning across 405,800 hectares (1 million acres), according to the regional forest fire center. S akha, Russia’s largest ethnic republic, had 36 active blazes covering 987,067 hectares (2.44 million acres) as of midnight Monday, federal authorities said . Russia’s Aerial Forest Protection Service said more than 1.3 million hectares (3.3 million acres) of wildfires were burning across Russia. Authorities have blamed the fires on summer heat and Siberian silk moth infestations, which have killed off vast swaths of trees and left behind highly flammable deadwood. The Krasnoyarsk region declared a wildfire emergency on June 10, barring the public from entering woodlands, lighting campfires, burning trash or grass and conducting any other fire-hazardous work. title: Russian Government Proposes Tax Relief for Wildberries and Sellers After Drone Attacks
text: Russian Government Proposes Tax Relief for Wildberries and Sellers After Drone Attacks Aug. 24, 2026 A Wildberries warehouse in Moscow region on fire after Ukrainian drone attack. REUTERS / Stringer The Russian government has drafted a financial assistance package for online retailer Wildberries and sellers who use the platform following weeks of Ukrainian attacks on the company’s warehouses and logistics centers, the Finance Ministry said Monday. Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said the proposed measures include a deferral of taxes and insurance payments, as well as a freeze on tax audits , all with the aim of “easing administrative and financial pressure” on impacted businesses. Under the draft proposal, sellers whose losses exceed 5% of annual revenue will receive a 12-month deferral on value-added tax (VAT), corporate tax and other liabilities due between August 2026 and July 2027. Following the deferral period, Wildberries sellers will be allowed to settle their tax obligations in equal monthly installments over 12 months.
